supported.quote: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and it does not handle the case where that list is empty, which is the ordinary case for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

With legacy-checkout-fallback off, more account page requests went through `render_spend_summary`'s monthly path into this division, raised ZeroDivisionError, and `serve_account_page` turned each one into a failed page.
It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching off a feature setting sent more shoppers' account pages through a spending calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases.

Account page requests that still reach the monthly spend summary could fail for shoppers with no purchases this month, and switching legacy-checkout-fallback off again would bring the same failures back.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load

Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of requests answered with server errors rose, and the service logged failed account page requests and warnings about the account page error rate.
Those account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, and the account page turned each error into a failed page.

At {P1.1} admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off. In the onset minute some account page requests already read the flag as off, every minute after that all of them did, and the ZeroDivisionError failures start in that same onset minute.
Some other flag change: the flag provider's history held a single change by anyone but Argus in the hour it read, and that change is this toggle.
Shoppers closing the connection: those errors were already logged before the onset, at a time when the flag was on and account pages rendered normally.

With the flag off, more account page requests went through render_spend_summary's monthly spend path, where average_spend_per_item_this_month divides by the number of this month's purchases, so it fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

No test was seen that covered average_spend_per_item_this_month, or render_spend_summary's monthly path, for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. The test file itself calls that the ordinary case.
The production change to legacy-checkout-fallback went from a share of requests to all of them almost at once. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen.
No check was seen that exercised account pages with legacy-checkout-fallback off before it was switched off in production.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called in to respond.
